messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: about output when using lavaan and multiple imputed data, and for multiple group
parts:
I am trying to use runMI

Hi Wilson,

To resolve this issue, you must install the latest development versions of lavaan:

install.packages("lavaan", repos="http://www.da.ugent.be", type="source")

and of semTools:

devtools::install_github("simsem/semTools/semTools")

Make sure to read the documentation on the ?runMI help page, as some arguments are no longer used.  

Yes, you can simply pass any lavaan() arguments (see the ?lavaan and ?lavOptions help pages), such as "group", "group.equal", and "group.partial" directly in the call to runMI().  That is the purpose of the "..." argument.

Make sure to also read the documentation for the anova() method on the class?runMI help page, which you can use to compare the fit of nested models to test invariance.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

Leslie,
The string 'fit' is not listed in the lavListInspect() help file as a valid value of the what parameter.  See the help file for a list of valid values for this parameter.  Note that the list is different from the valid values of the what parameter to lavInspect().

There may be a more elegant solution, but here is one strategy that you might try.  This is the example from the lavaanList help file with two changes: (1) the addition of the FUN parameter in the second last non-blank line and the printing to the console of the funList slot in the last line.

# The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

# a data generating function
generateData <- function() simulateData(HS.model, sample.nobs = 100)

set.seed(1234)
fit <- semList(HS.model, dataFunction = generateData, ndat = 5,
               store.slots = "partable", FUN=fitMeasures)

fit@funList


Keith
